name: career-technical-openquiz-python-ops-network
description: 按 Career OS 当前 JD 映射补充的公开技术测评题；题干、选项和解释均直接来自 Open Quiz Commons，不新增原创题。

source.selection_basis: Career OS jobs 表的 software-testing-ops、technical-support-fae、iot-embedded、data-analysis、ai-rag 题型缺口映射

questions.title: Which function from the os module returns the current working directory?
questions.explanation: os.getcwd() returns the current working directory as a string.
questions.source_text: Which function from the os module returns the current working directory?

questions.title: Which function from the os module changes the current working directory?
questions.explanation: os.chdir(path) changes the current working directory to the specified path.
questions.source_text: Which function from the os module changes the current working directory?

questions.title: Which attribute of the sys module gives the list of command-line arguments?
questions.explanation: sys.argv is a list containing the command-line arguments passed to the script.
questions.source_text: Which attribute of the sys module gives the list of command-line arguments?

questions.title: Which function from the os module is used to remove a file?
questions.explanation: os.remove(path) deletes the specified file.
questions.source_text: Which function from the os module is used to remove a file?

questions.title: Which function from the os module removes an empty directory?
questions.explanation: os.rmdir(path) removes an empty directory.
questions.source_text: Which function from the os module removes an empty directory?

questions.title: Which sys function terminates the program?
questions.explanation: sys.exit() raises SystemExit and terminates the program.
questions.source_text: Which sys function terminates the program?

questions.title: Which attribute of sys gives the version of Python being used?
questions.explanation: sys.version returns a string containing the Python version.
questions.source_text: Which attribute of sys gives the version of Python being used?

questions.title: Which function from the os module lists files and directories in a given path?
questions.explanation: os.listdir(path) returns a list of entries in the given directory.
questions.source_text: Which function from the os module lists files and directories in a given path?

questions.title: Which sys attribute gives the platform identifier?
questions.explanation: sys.platform returns a string identifying the operating system platform.
questions.source_text: Which sys attribute gives the platform identifier?

questions.title: Which os function is used to create a new directory?
questions.explanation: os.mkdir(path) creates a new directory at the specified path.
questions.source_text: Which os function is used to create a new directory?

questions.title: Which function is commonly used to run a command and capture its output?
questions.explanation: subprocess.run() executes a command and can capture output using the capture_output or stdout argument.
questions.source_text: Which function is commonly used to run a command and capture its output?

questions.title: Which argument of subprocess.run() ensures the command raises an exception if it fails?
questions.explanation: Using check=True makes subprocess.run() raise CalledProcessError if the command exits with a non-zero status.
questions.source_text: Which argument of subprocess.run() ensures the command raises an exception if it fails?

questions.title: Which class provides more fine-grained control over process creation and communication?
questions.explanation: subprocess.Popen allows advanced control over input, output, and process lifecycle.
questions.source_text: Which class provides more fine-grained control over process creation and communication?

questions.title: Which argument of subprocess.run() captures standard output?
questions.explanation: Setting stdout=subprocess.PIPE captures the command’s standard output.
questions.source_text: Which argument of subprocess.run() captures standard output?

questions.title: Which argument of subprocess.run() captures standard error?
questions.explanation: stderr=subprocess.PIPE captures the command’s standard error output.
questions.source_text: Which argument of subprocess.run() captures standard error?

questions.title: Which function is a simpler alternative to run() that only returns the exit code?
questions.explanation: subprocess.call() runs a command and returns its exit code.
questions.source_text: Which function is a simpler alternative to run() that only returns the exit code?

questions.title: Which attribute of CompletedProcess stores the exit status of the command?
questions.explanation: The returncode attribute indicates the exit status of the executed command.
questions.source_text: Which attribute of CompletedProcess stores the exit status of the command?

questions.title: Which method of Popen waits for the process to complete?
questions.explanation: The wait() method blocks until the process finishes and returns its exit code.
questions.source_text: Which method of Popen waits for the process to complete?

questions.title: Which method of Popen allows sending input and reading output/error streams?
questions.explanation: communicate() sends data to stdin and reads data from stdout and stderr.
questions.source_text: Which method of Popen allows sending input and reading output/error streams?

questions.title: Which argument of subprocess.run() executes the command through the shell?
questions.explanation: shell=True runs the command through the shell, allowing shell features like pipes and wildcards.
questions.source_text: Which argument of subprocess.run() executes the command through the shell?

questions.title: Which module in the Python standard library is the most low-level for handling HTTP client requests?
questions.explanation: `http.client` is a low-level HTTP protocol client; `urllib.request` is built on top of it, and `requests` is a third-party library.
questions.source_text: Which module in the Python standard library is the most low-level for handling HTTP client requests?

questions.title: In `urllib.request`, which function is used to open and fetch a URL?
questions.explanation: `urlopen()` is the primary function in `urllib.request` to open URLs, supporting HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP.
questions.source_text: In `urllib.request`, which function is used to open and fetch a URL?

questions.title: What is the default HTTP method used by `urllib.request.urlopen()` when the `data` parameter is `None`?
questions.explanation: By default, `urlopen` performs a GET request. If the `data` argument is provided, it performs a POST request.
questions.source_text: What is the default HTTP method used by `urllib.request.urlopen()` when the `data` parameter is `None`?

questions.title: Which class in the `http.server` module can be used to create a basic web server that serves files from the current directory?
questions.explanation: `SimpleHTTPRequestHandler` maps HTTP requests to the local directory structure and is often used via `python -m http.server`.
questions.source_text: Which class in the `http.server` module can be used to create a basic web server that serves files from the current directory?

questions.title: How do you access the HTTP status code from a response object returned by `urllib.request.urlopen(url)`?
questions.explanation: The `getcode()` method (or the `status` attribute in newer Python 3 versions) returns the HTTP status code of the response.
questions.source_text: How do you access the HTTP status code from a response object returned by `urllib.request.urlopen(url)`?

questions.title: Which header must be set to send JSON data in a POST request so the server understands the format?
questions.explanation: The `Content-Type` header tells the server the media type of the body of the request.
questions.source_text: Which header must be set to send JSON data in a POST request so the server understands the format?

questions.title: When using `urllib.parse`, which function is used to convert a dictionary into a URL-encoded query string?
questions.explanation: `urlencode()` takes a mapping or sequence of two-element tuples and converts it into a 'percent-encoded' string.
questions.source_text: When using `urllib.parse`, which function is used to convert a dictionary into a URL-encoded query string?

questions.title: In the `http.client` module, which method must be called to send the actual request to the server after `putrequest` and `putheader`?
questions.explanation: `endheaders()` sends a blank line indicating the end of the HTTP headers, followed by `send()` for the body if necessary.
questions.source_text: In the `http.client` module, which method must be called to send the actual request to the server after `putrequest` and `putheader`?

questions.title: What is the purpose of the `urllib.robotparser` module?
options: B. To parse robots.txt files and check if a spider can fetch a URL
C. To detect if a client is a bot
questions.explanation: `robotparser` provides a single class, `RobotFileParser`, which answers questions about whether a particular user agent can fetch a URL on a website.
questions.source_text: What is the purpose of the `urllib.robotparser` module?

questions.title: What happens if you call `read()` on an HTTP response object in Python without specifying a size?
options: B. It reads the entire response body
D. It reads only the headers
questions.explanation: The `read()` method reads the entire content of the response body unless a byte count is specified.
questions.source_text: What happens if you call `read()` on an HTTP response object in Python without specifying a size?

questions.title: Which exception is typically raised by `urllib.request` when an HTTP error occurs (like 404 or 500)?
questions.explanation: `HTTPError` is a subclass of `URLError` specifically raised for exotic HTTP errors.
questions.source_text: Which exception is typically raised by `urllib.request` when an HTTP error occurs (like 404 or 500)?

questions.title: How can you pass custom headers (like a User-Agent) using `urllib.request`?
options: A. Pass a headers dict to urlopen()
B. Use the Request object: urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers)
C. Use the set_header() global function
D. Headers cannot be customized in urllib
questions.explanation: To customize headers, you must instantiate a `urllib.request.Request` object with the headers dictionary and pass that object to `urlopen()`.
questions.source_text: How can you pass custom headers (like a User-Agent) using `urllib.request`?

questions.title: Which module in the Python standard library provides access to the BSD socket interface?
questions.explanation: The `socket` module provides the core interface for network communications, allowing for low-level socket operations.
questions.source_text: Which module in the Python standard library provides access to the BSD socket interface?

questions.title: What address family is used for IPv4 networking in Python sockets?
questions.explanation: `AF_INET` refers to the address family for IPv4. `AF_INET6` is used for IPv6, and `AF_UNIX` is for local inter-process communication.
questions.source_text: What address family is used for IPv4 networking in Python sockets?

questions.title: Which socket type is used to create a TCP (connection-oriented) socket?
questions.explanation: `SOCK_STREAM` is the socket type for TCP, providing sequenced, reliable, two-way, connection-based byte streams.
questions.source_text: Which socket type is used to create a TCP (connection-oriented) socket?

questions.title: What is the purpose of the `bind()` method in a server-side socket?
options: A. To connect to a remote host
B. To listen for incoming connections
C. To associate the socket with a specific network interface and port
D. To send data to a client
questions.explanation: `bind()` assigns a local IP address and port number to a socket, which is necessary for a server to accept connections on that port.
questions.source_text: What is the purpose of the `bind()` method in a server-side socket?

questions.title: Which method is used by a TCP server to accept an incoming connection request?
questions.explanation: `accept()` blocks and waits for an incoming connection. When a client connects, it returns a new socket object representing the connection and the client's address.
questions.source_text: Which method is used by a TCP server to accept an incoming connection request?

questions.title: In a UDP socket, which method is typically used to send data because it does not require a prior connection?
questions.explanation: `sendto()` is used for UDP (connectionless) sockets to send data to a specific address, as no permanent connection is established.
questions.source_text: In a UDP socket, which method is typically used to send data because it does not require a prior connection?

questions.title: What does the `listen(backlog)` method do in a TCP server?
options: A. It starts the data transfer
B. It sets the maximum number of queued unaccepted connections
C. It determines how many seconds to wait for a connection
D. It creates a new thread for every client
questions.explanation: The `backlog` parameter specifies the number of unaccepted connections that the system will allow to queue up before refusing new ones.
questions.source_text: What does the `listen(backlog)` method do in a TCP server?

questions.title: What is the difference between `recv()` and `recvfrom()`?
options: B. `recv()` is for TCP; `recvfrom()` is for UDP and returns the sender's address
D. `recv()` is for sending and `recvfrom()` is for receiving
questions.explanation: `recvfrom()` is typically used with UDP sockets because it returns both the data and the address of the sender, which is necessary to reply.
questions.source_text: What is the difference between `recv()` and `recvfrom()`?

questions.title: Which method ensures that all data in a buffer is sent before returning, potentially making multiple low-level calls?
questions.explanation: Unlike `send()`, which might send only part of the data, `sendall()` continues to send data until either the entire message is transmitted or an error occurs.
questions.source_text: Which method ensures that all data in a buffer is sent before returning, potentially making multiple low-level calls?

questions.title: What is the standard way to close a socket connection to free up resources?
questions.explanation: The `close()` method terminates the socket connection and releases the associated file descriptor and system resources.
questions.source_text: What is the standard way to close a socket connection to free up resources?

questions.title: When using `socket.gethostname()`, what information is retrieved?
options: A. The IP address of the current machine
B. The hostname of the current machine
C. The hostnames of all connected clients
questions.explanation: `gethostname()` returns a string containing the hostname of the machine where the Python interpreter is currently executing.
questions.source_text: When using `socket.gethostname()`, what information is retrieved?

questions.title: Which of the following creates a non-blocking socket?
questions.explanation: In Python, `setblocking(False)` is a shorthand for `settimeout(0.0)`. Both make the socket operations return immediately with an error if they cannot complete.
questions.source_text: Which of the following creates a non-blocking socket?
